questions.prompt: Which concept bundles data and methods and controls access to them?
questions.explanation: Encapsulation combines state and behaviour and restricts direct access.

questions.prompt: What allows a subclass to provide its own version of a parent method?
questions.explanation: Overriding replaces the inherited implementation and enables runtime polymorphism.
Composition means an object contains other objects as parts.

questions.prompt: The Liskov Substitution Principle states that:
options: Subtypes must be usable wherever the base type is expected without breaking correctness
A class should have only one reason to change
High-level modules should not depend on low-level modules
Clients should not depend on methods they do not use
questions.explanation: LSP concerns behavioural substitutability of subtypes.
